operational-example.copy: Use Chart Panel to frame one operational visualization with title, context, summary value, and actions.

scenario.title: Operational charts
scenario.meta: Compact visualization cards with Flow semantics
rationale: Chart Panel frames one visualization before it becomes a dashboard pattern.
ZIP parity is applied to card geometry, compact hierarchy, chart density, and reveal motion while Flow keeps semantic color.
Use a pattern when multiple panels need shared filters, layout rules, or navigation.

items.rule: Frames one Charts primitive instance with stable spacing, border, density, and responsive width.
Names the metric and preserves compact overline hierarchy.
Exposes the main reading as text before the visualization.
Produces echartsOption, textSummary, legendModel, and tableFallback so rendering can hydrate with Apache ECharts or fall back safely.
Renders a compact Flow fallback when ECharts is unavailable, without changing the data model.
Clarifies period, unit, or comparison only when needed.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, error, warning, focus, hover, default
items: Provide a readable chart title and accessible image label.
Expose the key value in text, not only in the visualization.
Keep warning and error states text-backed.
Preserve focus visibility when chart actions are present.
Respect reduced motion for animated chart reveals.

variants.copy: Chart Panel variants map the ZIP visualization families that fit inside one self-contained Flow component: sparkline, bars, line, area, donut, Pareto, bullet, comparison, and compact.

states.copy: Chart Panel states communicate availability, attention, focus, hover, and error without changing the metric meaning.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant defines the visualization treatment; state defines feedback and availability without rewriting the data story.

full-width.copy: Chart Panel can fill its parent in analytics layouts, but the plot keeps a useful minimum reading area.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Use one readable chart per row on small viewports and avoid shrinking plots below their useful reading width.

viewport-organization.copy: Chart Panel should use available width before adding more columns because dense charts lose meaning quickly.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Use compact charts with visible value and caption.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Use one or two panels only when both remain readable.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Let critical charts breathe before arranging dense grids.

playground.copy: Use the playground to verify title, summary value, variant, state, and chart readability before composing dashboards.

api-foundations.copy: Chart Panel API frames the Charts primitive. The primitive owns echartsOption, textSummary, legendModel, and tableFallback; the component owns the card frame, state, density, and accessible fallback.

props.name: values
props.notes: Local chart values rendered inside the component.

props.name: labels
props.notes: Optional labels for chart values, used by donut, bullet, bars, and accessible titles.

props.name: segments
props.notes: Optional part-to-whole data for donut panels.

props.name: variant
props.notes: Local visualization treatment: sparkline, bars, line, area, donut, pareto, bullet, comparison, or compact.

props.name: state
props.notes: Visual state: default, focus, hover, warning, error, or disabled.

props.name: tone
props.notes: Semantic tone for value and plot emphasis.

props.name: fullWidth
props.notes: Lets the panel fill its parent grid column.

props.name: series
props.notes: Multi-series values passed into the Charts primitive for line and comparison panels.

props.name: comparisons
props.notes: Paired series passed into the Charts primitive for grouped comparison panels.

props.name: valueLabels
props.notes: Optional formatted labels used by fallback marks and tooltips while raw values remain numeric.

groups.title: Use
items: Keep the key value readable as text.
Escalate to patterns for multi-chart dashboards.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not use as a decorative chart frame.
Do not shrink plots until labels disappear.
Do not encode risk with color only.

groups.title: Review
items: Check contrast in all chart states.
Check that title and caption explain the data.

mustTest: Charts primitive emits echartsOption, textSummary, legendModel, and tableFallback
ECharts hydration keeps Flow fallback available when the library is missing
Fallback marks expose hover and focus tooltip data.
Motion uses Flow duration/easing and does not auto-open any tooltip.
rejectIf: The chart has no readable title.
The summary value only exists inside pixels.
The plot is miniaturized until unreadable.
Raw colors or motion values are used.
Bars render without value/axis labels when the variant needs them.
Sparkline, bars, Pareto, bullet, donut, or comparison collapse into the same generic chart.
Chart Panel renders charts without going through the Charts primitive.
ECharts option and fallback disagree on values or labels.
Demos use placeholder values that read as decorative images.
Interactive chart marks cannot be reached by keyboard.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Chart Panel as a Flow frame around the Charts primitive. Agents may place it when the metric is known, but humans confirm data meaning, comparison period, and whether Apache ECharts hydration is required.
canDecide: Use Chart Panel for one trend, comparison, or KPI visualization.
Choose compact only when the summary value carries the main meaning.
Use warning or error when the metric needs operational attention.
mustAsk: The chart changes financial or safety decisions.
Multiple charts need shared filters or layout rules.
The data source, unit, or comparison period is unclear.
miel.handoff: I am using Chart Panel for one operational visualization. Please confirm metric, source, period, accessible summary, and whether this belongs in a dashboard pattern.
